title: 9. Why Pluto is a Dwarf Planet (VERY FREQUENTLY ASKED)

blocks.content: Pluto failed to satisfy the third condition: it has not cleared the neighborhood around its orbit.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: In August 2006, the International Astronomical Union (IAU) redefined the official criteria required for a celestial body to be designated as a planet.
To be a planet, an object must orbit the Sun, have sufficient mass to be spherical (hydrostatic equilibrium), and clear the neighborhood around its orbit.
Pluto meets the first two criteria but fails the third because its gravity is not strong enough to clear debris and other objects from its orbital neighborhood.
Pluto resides in the Kuiper Belt, sharing its orbital region with thousands of other icy objects and periodically crossing the path of Neptune.

rows: No (Shares path with Kuiper Belt objects)
Is a satellite/moon of another planet

items: The official decision to downgrade Pluto was made by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) in August 2006 in Prague.
Examiners frequently ask which specific condition Pluto failed: 'Clearing the neighborhood around its orbit'.
Pluto is located in the Kuiper Belt and is now officially designated as minor planet 134340 Pluto.
